permutationLabel: Elderly (79) on warfarin (INR 2.6) — ASGE high risk; anticoagulation plan before sphincterotomy
summary: 79-year-old man with AF on warfarin (INR 2.6): painless-ish jaundice with RUQ discomfort; bilirubin 70, ALP 360; ultrasound shows a 12 mm CBD with stones; afebrile.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Jaundice with right upper abdominal discomfort
inputs.hpi: Four days of yellow eyes with right upper quadrant discomfort, dark urine and pale stools. No fever or rigors. Atrial fibrillation on warfarin (target INR 2–3), hypertension, type 2 diabetes on metformin. Previous stroke 2021.

exam.general: Jaundiced. Irregularly irregular pulse 88/min, BP 146/84, temperature 36.9°C.
exam.abdomen: Mild right upper quadrant tenderness. No palpable gallbladder.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Gallstones. CBD dilated to 12 mm containing several shadowing stones (largest 9 mm). Intrahepatic duct dilatation. No pancreatic mass seen.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Choledocholithiasis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Choledocholithiasis — ASGE 2019 high risk (duct stones on ultrasound, bilirubin 70 µmol/L with CBD 12 mm). No cholangitis. On warfarin, INR 2.6.

mustNotMiss.note: Age 79 with obstructive jaundice: malignancy must stay in the differential.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: choledocholithiasis, inguinal hernia, cholecystitis — no malignant cause for obstructive jaundice at 79 (symptom inference #4 has one). | iOS CI 2026-09-25 (run 36169134350, database mode): not in top 5 of ios.bayes: 1. Choledocholithiasis | 2. Ascending Cholangitis | 3. Liver Cirrhosis (Decompensated) | 4. Acute Pancreatitis | 5. Acute Appendicitis
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: age modifier for pancreatic/biliary malignancy with jaundice; recalibrate the inguinal hernia prior (0.15) that fills the top 3 in unrelated presentations.

redFlags.note: Therapeutic INR before a high-bleeding-risk sphincterotomy.

mustInclude.note: BSG/ESGE 2021: ERCP with sphincterotomy is a high-risk procedure — stop warfarin 5 days before and check INR <1.5 (bridging not needed for AF without other high-risk features). Proceeding with INR 2.6 risks post-sphincterotomy haemorrhage.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ASGE guideline on the role of endoscopy in the evaluation and management of choledocholithiasis
guideline.section: Risk strata. High: CBD stone on US/cross-sectional imaging, or total bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD, or ascending cholangitis → ERCP. Intermediate: abnormal liver tests, age >55, or dilated CBD → EUS/MRCP or intra-operative cholangiography/laparoscopic US. Low: none → cholecystectomy without further CBD evaluation
guideline.citation: Buxbaum JL, Abbas Fehmi SM, Sultan S, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2019;89:1075–1105.e15.

guideline.name: BSG/ESGE guideline — endoscopy in patients on antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy (2021 update)
guideline.section: ERCP with sphincterotomy is a high-risk procedure: stop warfarin 5 days before and check INR <1.5; bridging only for high thrombotic risk; DOACs stopped per renal function
guideline.citation: Veitch AM, Radaelli F, Alikhan R, et al. Gut. 2021;70:1611–1628.

rationale: Permutation: elderly anticoagulated patient. The diagnosis and ERCP indication are unchanged; the safety content is the peri-procedural anticoagulation plan and keeping malignancy in the differential at 79.
